title: Windows BitLocker RCE Flaw Lets Attackers Execute Malicious Code on Windows Systems
content_md: Microsoft has released security updates for CVE-2026-69449, a Windows BitLocker remote code execution vulnerability caused by a heap-based buffer overflow. The issue, could allow an authorized attacker to execute malicious code on affected Windows systems and, in certain network scenarios, potentially achieve remote code execution. The vulnerability was disclosed on September 8, 2026, as part of Microsoft’s latest security update release. Windows BitLocker RCE Flaw Microsoft assigned the flaw CWE-122, identifying it as a heap-based buffer overflow a memory-safety weakness that can occur when software writes more data to a heap-allocated buffer than it is designed to hold. According to Microsoft’s advisory , successful exploitation could enable an attacker to gain remote code execution through an in-network attack involving arbitrary endpoint calls. Microsoft’s executive summary also describes the threat as requiring an authorized attacker to execute code locally. The vulnerability is not presented as an unauthenticated, internet-exposed wormable flaw. However, an attacker who has already obtained valid access to a Windows environment or who can operate from a trusted internal network position could use the vulnerable BitLocker component as part of a broader intrusion chain. Heap corruption vulnerabilities are particularly significant because they can provide attackers with a path to manipulate program execution.
